newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist Emmanuelli blasts Vilvoorde move.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist Emmanuelli blasts Vilvoorde move.

text.p: Leading French Socialist Henri Emmanuelli added his voice on Tuesday to a chorus of attacks on Renault for proceeding with the closure of a Belgian car assembly plant.
Emmanuelli, head of the National Assembly finance committee, said Renault did not seem to have seriously considered reducing the working week to save jobs and its plans would boost state expenses.

"Renault should seriously examine reducing work weeks ... I'm not sure that would not be less expensive than what we're doing today. By saying there won't be layoffs, it means the bill will be quite large," he told France Inter radio.
He criticised companies which shifted costs onto the state and the taxpayer to preserve profitability.

Renault, which confirmed on Saturday that it would close the Vilvoorde plant, has said reducing schedules would not generate as many savings -- about 850 million francs a year -- as a closure. The money-losing company also said it needs to streamline its production sites, which are smaller and more dispersed than those of its rivals in Europe.
An independent consultant, brought in by the company nine days after the Socialists were elected to power, agreed that the plant should be closed.
Renault, 46 percent state-owned, announced in February that it would close the plant, which then employed 3,100 people, and said in March it would cut some 2,800 jobs in France this year.
The reaffirmation of its earlier decision despite the outcry in France and Belgium is embarrassing for the new Socialist-led government, which had attacked the shutdown and promised to preserve jobs.
An aide to Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Monday that Jospin disagreed with the decision but felt the case was too far gone to push for a reversal.
